The security team also needs findings for instances that are publicly reachable only in two restricted regions, and wants to ignore instances in maintenance. What should it do?

choices.text: Modify the predefined detector's logic in place so that it also checks the region property, then re-enable the changed detector for the organization's projects
Write an organization policy custom constraint, since constraints generate findings in Security Command Center for existing resources
Create a Security Health Analytics custom module whose CEL condition checks the region and state of Cloud SQL instances, and send its findings to Security Command Center
Export Cloud SQL instance configuration to Cloud Storage every night and have an analyst filter the exported files by region and state

stem: A security team adopts a requirement that every new GKE cluster must have a specific hardening setting. Several existing clusters already violate it. The team wants to stop new violations without disrupting current clusters and also to see the existing ones. What combination fits?

choices.text: A Binary Authorization policy on each cluster, because it blocks the creation of other clusters whose settings are non-compliant
A custom organization policy constraint alone, because newly enforced constraints reconfigure every existing cluster that violates them
A Security Health Analytics custom module alone, because its findings prevent the creation of any non-compliant cluster in the whole organization
A custom organization policy constraint for cluster creation, tested first in dry-run mode, plus a Security Health Analytics custom module for existing ones

stem: A company keeps internal Python packages in an Artifact Registry standard repository and proxies the public package index through a remote repository. Developers install through one virtual repository. A security review warns that an attacker could publish a public package with the same name as an internal one and a higher version number. How should the virtual repository be configured?

choices.text: Give both upstream repositories the same priority so that Artifact Registry serves the highest version it finds in either of them
Give the internal standard repository a higher priority than the remote repository so that Artifact Registry searches it first for any requested package
Remove the virtual repository and let each developer install directly from both sources, using an index-url flag on every command
Give the remote repository the higher priority so developers receive the latest public fixes before any internal package is even considered by the repository

stem: During an incident the team turns on logging for an existing firewall policy allow rule that matches SSH to a bastion VM. An engineer's SSH session opened before the change stays active and busy, and the log shows no entry for it, although sessions opened afterwards are logged. What explains this?

choices.text: Firewall policy rules logging skips TCP connections that carry interactive traffic, which is why such sessions never produce entries
Logging records a connection when it is established, so a connection that already existed is logged only after it has been idle for at least 10 minutes
Allow rules log only the first connection from each source address per day, so the engineer's address was counted before the change was made
The entry for the session is delayed until the connection closes, and it is then written to the audit log together with the final byte counts

stem: Incident responders suspect that a compromised VM keeps one long-lived TCP connection open to an external server and transfers data over hours. Cloud NGFW firewall policy logging on the matching allow rule shows a single entry from the start of the connection. How can the team continue to see how the traffic evolves over time?

choices.text: Use VPC Flow Logs, which sample packets and write aggregated flow records for each interval for as long as the connection carries traffic
Replace the allow rule with a deny rule, because deny logging is written only once for each connection that it drops
Increase the verbosity of the firewall policy rule log, because a single rule can write continuous entries for every connection it allows
Enable Cloud Audit Logs data access logging for Compute Engine, which records packet counts for each network connection of the VM

stem: A company continuously creates new projects, each with its own VPC networks. The security team needs flow records from every subnet, every Cloud VPN tunnel and every VLAN attachment for forensics, including those in projects that do not exist yet. What is the most reliable way?

choices.text: Enable flow logs on each subnet with a script run at project creation, and ask project owners to enable them on VPN tunnels manually
Configure Packet Mirroring on every subnet and keep the mirrored packets in a collector as the forensic record for the organization
Enable VPC Flow Logs with an organization-level configuration covering all subnets, VLAN attachments and Cloud VPN tunnels of every VPC network
Enable firewall policy rules logging on every rule, because it also records traffic that crosses Cloud VPN tunnels and VLAN attachments

stem: A security team investigating a port scan finds that VPC Flow Logs show almost none of the short TCP probes that a scanning VM sent to other VMs, because each probe is only one or two packets. The team needs a record of every outbound TCP connection attempt. What should it enable?

choices.text: A 15-minute aggregation interval, so that all packets of each flow are combined into a single entry
Firewall Rules Logging on the implied allow egress rule, so that each outgoing connection is logged
TCP connection logging, an optional flow logs setting that logs connection setup (SYN) events
A primary sampling rate of 1.0 on the subnet, so that every packet of every flow is sampled and logged

stem: A forensics team needs complete packet payloads from web-tier VMs in one subnet to analyze with a third-party network detection appliance running on Compute Engine. Which TWO statements about the design are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Filters on the policy for protocol, CIDR range and direction, so only the traffic of interest is cloned and the extra VM bandwidth stays limited
VPC Flow Logs with full secondary sampling and all metadata fields, because flow records carry the payload bytes of every sampled packet
A Cloud IDS endpoint in each zone, because Cloud IDS forwards copies of the packet payloads to customer-owned inspection appliances
A Cloud NAT gateway for the appliance, because mirrored traffic must reach the collector through a public IP address of the gateway
A Packet Mirroring policy with mirrored sources and a collector instance group behind an internal passthrough load balancer whose forwarding rule is for mirroring

stem: A forensics team created one Packet Mirroring policy to mirror web VMs in us-central1 and in europe-west1 of the same VPC network to a single collector group in us-central1. The policy cannot be created. What explains this and what is the fix?

choices.text: A policy can select sources only by network tag in more than one region, so replace the subnet selection with tags for both regions
All mirrored sources of a policy must be in one region and the collector in that same region, so create one policy and collector per region
A policy can mirror only ingress traffic when its sources span regions, so drop egress mirroring and keep the single collector
A collector must sit behind an external passthrough load balancer to receive traffic across regions, so switch the load balancer type

stem: A security team has configured a Cloud IDS endpoint with a packet mirroring policy for a subnet, and also has a Cloud NGFW Layer 7 inspection firewall policy rule for the same traffic. The IDS endpoint shows no threat alerts for the matching traffic. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The two policies cover the same traffic and Layer 7 inspection takes priority, so that traffic is not mirrored to IDS
The threat log stays empty until a minimum alert severity of Critical is chosen for the endpoint's signature set
Cloud IDS needs firewall rule logging turned off on the matching rule before it starts analyzing that connection
Cloud IDS and Cloud NGFW Layer 7 inspection are not supported in the same VPC network, so the endpoint is paused

stem: A Cloud IDS endpoint produces many alerts for one signature that the application team has confirmed is a false positive for its legitimate scanner. The security team does not want to lose detection for other threats. What should it do?

choices.text: Delete the endpoint and recreate it in another region so that the signature database starts without the noisy signature
Set the minimum severity of the endpoint to Critical, believing that this filters out only the one noisy signature and nothing else
Remove the packet mirroring policy for the scanner's subnet so no traffic from it is mirrored, including traffic unrelated to the scanner at all
Add the signature's threat ID to the endpoint's threat exceptions, found from the threat logs, and keep the default signature set for everything else

stem: Analysts need to find the top talkers by hour across several months of VPC Flow Logs, using SQL aggregations, without exporting a second copy of the logs to another service. What should the security engineer set up?

choices.text: Enable Packet Mirroring so that a collector appliance counts the bytes per source IP address for each hour and stores the totals
Upgrade the flow log bucket to use analytics (Log Analytics, now Observability Analytics) and query it with SQL, optionally via a linked BigQuery dataset
Query the logs in Logs Explorer using aggregate functions, because Logs Explorer supports counting and grouping log entries by the hour and source address
Create a log-based counter metric for each source IP address and graph the metric values for each hour across the retention period

stem: Network logs are stored in a log bucket upgraded to analytics, and the bucket has field-level access controls that hide source IP addresses from a group of junior analysts. The team proposes giving the juniors access to the bucket's linked BigQuery dataset so they can use their BigQuery skills. What is the problem?

choices.text: BigQuery does not honor the log bucket's field-level access controls, so anyone who can query the linked dataset can read all fields, including the hidden addresses
A linked BigQuery dataset can be created only for buckets that have no field-level access controls, so the proposal cannot even be configured by the team
The linked dataset shows the restricted fields as masked, but the masking is lost whenever the analysts export their query results
Junior analysts cannot run SQL on a linked dataset unless the bucket contents are also exported to a Cloud Storage bucket

stem: A team compares Cloud NGFW firewall policy rules logging with VPC Flow Logs for network investigations. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: VPC Flow Logs capture complete packet payloads for each sampled connection, which analysts can replay for forensic review
Firewall policy rules logging writes one separate log entry for every packet of an allowed connection while it lasts
Firewall policy rules logging records a connection and the rule that applied to it, which shows whether a particular rule allowed or denied the traffic
Firewall policy rules logging records every IP protocol, including ICMP and ESP, for all rules of every firewall policy type in the organization
VPC Flow Logs sample packets and aggregate them by IP connection, so they estimate totals and suit monitoring and forensics rather than exact accounting

stem: Data Access audit logs for `DATA_READ` on Cloud Storage are enabled organization-wide for compliance. A nightly integrity-scan job running as the service account `scan@sec-tools.iam.gserviceaccount.com` reads millions of objects and now generates most of the log volume and cost. Auditors must still see every read by all other principals. What should the security engineer do?

choices.text: Grant the scan service account the Private Logs Viewer role, because the role stops the principal's reads from being written
Disable DATA_READ for Cloud Storage in the audit configuration of the project that hosts the scan job, leaving the organization setting as it is
Add an exclusion filter to the `_Required` sink that drops the scan job's entries, because that sink stores Data Access logs
Add the scan service account as an exempted principal in the Cloud Storage audit configuration, keeping DATA_READ on for everyone else

stem: A platform team creates an intercepting aggregated sink at the organization level. Its filter matches all log entries that originate in projects under the `apps` folder, and it routes them to a central security project. Afterwards the application owners report that Logs Explorer in their own projects no longer shows application logs, although Admin Activity audit entries still appear. What explains this, and what is the fix?

choices.text: The `_Required` bucket of each project now rejects writes from applications, so its retention must be set to a longer period
The sink's writer identity lacks the Logs Bucket Writer role, so it must be granted on every source project's `_Default` bucket
The sink intercepts, so matching entries skip child sinks such as `_Default`; recreate it as a non-intercepting sink
Application owners need the Private Logs Viewer role, because entries routed by a sink are treated as private logs in their own projects

stem: An organization-level aggregated sink routes audit logs to a Cloud Storage bucket in a project that is inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter. The sink was created without errors, but no objects arrive in the bucket. Perimeter violation logs show denied writes from the sink's service account. How should the security engineer fix this?

choices.text: Move the Cloud Storage bucket outside the perimeter permanently, because log sinks cannot write to any resource that a perimeter protects
Add an ingress rule to the perimeter that allows access from the sink's service account, using ANY_IDENTITY as the identity type for this destination
Add an ingress rule with the identity type ANY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, which covers the sink's service account because it is a Google-managed identity
Add an egress rule so that the source projects, which are outside the perimeter, may call Cloud Storage in the destination project

stem: A central security project stores logs from 12 workload projects in one custom log bucket. Each team lead must read only the entries of their own project, and nobody besides the security team may read the others. What is the most appropriate way to grant this access?

choices.text: Create one log view per project on the bucket, then grant each team lead the Log View Accessor role on only their view
Grant each team lead access to the bucket's `_AllLogs` view and attach an IAM condition on the project ID to the binding
Grant each team lead the Log View Accessor role on the central security project, then remind them to filter by project in queries
Create twelve separate log buckets in the central project and give every team lead the Logs Viewer role on that project

stem: An external auditor was granted the Logs Viewer role on a project. The auditor can see Admin Activity audit entries in the `_Default` bucket but cannot find any Data Access audit entries, although the security team confirmed that Data Access logs are enabled and flowing. Which change meets the auditor's need with least privilege?

choices.text: Grant the auditor the Logs Viewer role on the organization instead of the project
Grant the auditor the Logs Configuration Writer role so the auditor can inspect the `_Default` sink
Grant the auditor the Logging Admin role on the project, which includes all log read permissions
Grant the auditor the Private Logs Viewer role on the project

stem: Company policy requires that every new Cloud Logging bucket in any project of the organization is encrypted with a customer-managed key from the EU region. Security wants the rule to apply automatically, including to buckets that teams create later. What should the security engineer do?

choices.text: Configure CMEK on the central destination bucket only, because entries routed there inherit the key of the source projects
Ask each team to configure CMEK on its `_Default` bucket after it is created, then audit the buckets quarterly
Create a global key and reference it in default settings, since keys in the `global` location can protect log buckets in any region and satisfy residency
Set organization default resource settings for Cloud Logging with an EU Cloud KMS key and create buckets in the matching location

stem: An investigation team must be able to show regulators that security logs in a central bucket were retained for seven years and could not be shortened or erased by administrators, including project owners. Which configuration provides this?

choices.text: Set seven-year retention on the bucket and lock it, so retention cannot be reduced and the bucket cannot be deleted early
Add an exclusion filter on the `_Default` sink that drops entries from the bucket before their retention period elapses
Set the retention period to seven years and rely on IAM to prevent anyone from holding the permission to change retention
Route the logs to the `_Required` bucket, whose fixed retention period is applied automatically to every entry routed there by a sink

stem: Which TWO events are recorded in Cloud Audit Logs automatically, without any audit configuration being enabled, and cannot be switched off by the project's own audit configuration? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A user reads the contents of an object in a Cloud Storage bucket
A user's request is blocked because it violates a VPC Service Controls perimeter
A service reads a Secret Manager secret value in a project
A principal calls an API that only reads a resource's metadata
The autoscaler adds a VM to a managed instance group in response to load

stem: A SIEM license is priced per ingested gigabyte. The security operations team needs near-real-time audit events from every project in the organization, including new ones, but cannot afford to send all logs. Full copies must remain searchable inside Google Cloud for investigations. Which TWO actions fit? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Disable Data Access logging organization-wide so fewer entries exist for the SIEM to receive
Create a sink in each project that routes to Cloud Storage, and have the SIEM import the files from each bucket every hour
Create an organization-level aggregated sink with an inclusion filter on audit logs that routes to a Pub/Sub topic read by the SIEM
Route all organization logs to Pub/Sub without a filter so the SIEM can apply its own drop rules at ingestion
Leave the default sinks in place so the full log set stays in log buckets, and do not add exclusions to them

stem: A team adds an exclusion filter to the `_Default` sink to drop verbose Data Access entries from the `_Default` bucket and cut storage. The next week, the security team asks whether the organization-level sink that feeds the SIEM will still receive those entries. What is true?

choices.text: The SIEM feed is unaffected only if the exclusion filter is deleted, because a sink with exclusions always blocks routing to other destinations
The SIEM feed is unaffected, because each sink applies its own filters independently and the exclusion belongs only to the `_Default` sink
The SIEM feed loses the entries, because an exclusion removes entries from the Log Router before any other sink processes them
The SIEM feed loses the entries, because exclusions in `_Default` apply to all sinks in the same project and to every aggregated sink above it

stem: The security team must be notified within minutes whenever the break-glass account `breakglass-admin@example.com` performs any Google Cloud administrative action, in any project. The account is normally dormant. What is the best detection design?

choices.text: Aggregate audit logs of all projects in one central project, then enable Data Access audit logs for that account because Admin Activity is not written
Aggregate audit logs of all projects in one central project, then mute that principal's Security Command Center findings and review them monthly
Aggregate audit logs of all projects in one central project, then add a log-based alert there on Admin Activity entries from that principal
Aggregate audit logs of all projects in one central project, then run a saved Logs Explorer query for that principal during each weekly meeting

stem: A sandbox folder intentionally contains buckets with public demo data, approved by the CISO for 60 days. Security Health Analytics reports public-bucket findings for them every day and analysts are overwhelmed. The same findings must continue to appear for every other folder. What should the security engineer do?

choices.text: Create a dynamic mute rule scoped to the sandbox folder's findings with an expiration of 60 days
Delete the sandbox projects' findings from the list; the detector then skips resources it has scanned before
Disable the public-bucket detector for the whole organization until the demo period has finished
Set each finding's state to INACTIVE manually, because inactive findings stay hidden until the 60 days expire

stem: A team has an old static mute rule hiding all open-firewall findings in project `lab-1`. Last month it added a dynamic mute rule for the same findings with a 30-day expiry. The 30 days have passed, but the findings are still muted. What is the explanation and the right fix?

choices.text: Mute rules at project level cannot expire; the rule must be recreated at organization level for the expiry to take effect
Dynamic mute rules never expire for findings that were already muted once, so an analyst must unmute each finding by hand
The dynamic rule expired but Security Command Center caches the mute state for a year, so only re-enabling the detector clears it
The static rule takes precedence over the dynamic rule and keeps muting; remove the static rule and use dynamic mute rules only

stem: A security team wants new HIGH and CRITICAL Security Command Center findings to start an automated response in near real time. Data residency is enabled and findings are stored in the `eu` location. Which TWO design elements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create a log sink on the Security Command Center API that publishes every new finding as a file into a Cloud Storage bucket
Export findings to BigQuery and trigger the response when a scheduled query finds new rows each hour
Poll the findings list API every few seconds from a script and keep the last timestamp in a variable
Create the export configuration in the `eu` location, the same Security Command Center location as the findings
Configure a continuous export to Pub/Sub with a filter such as active, non-muted findings of HIGH or CRITICAL severity

stem: Security wants Security Command Center to alert on a service account that lists its own IAM policy, a sign of reconnaissance with stolen credentials. Event Threat Detection is active at the organization, but no `Discovery: Service Account Self-Investigation` findings ever appear, even after a test. Admin Activity logs are present. What is the likely cause and fix?

choices.text: Event Threat Detection reads only Admin Activity logs, so the rule can never trigger and a custom log alert is needed instead
The detector reads IAM Data Access audit logs, which are off by default; enable the DATA_READ type for the IAM service
The test happened inside a project that contains no `_Default` bucket, so the findings are stored in `_Required`
Findings are generated only if the service account has the Security Center Admin role, which the test account lacks

stem: At 02:10 a Security Command Center finding reports that a service account key was used from an unfamiliar IP address to download data from a bucket. The incident response lead needs the correct first sequence. Which approach follows incident response practice for this situation?

choices.text: Mute the finding to avoid duplicate alerts, then review the activity at the next scheduled access review
Wait for a second finding to confirm the incident, because acting on a single finding risks disrupting production
Disable the compromised key, preserve audit logs and affected resources, then investigate scope and rotate credentials
Delete the service account and its project immediately so that no further access is possible, then restore everything from backup

stem: A security analyst reviews three observations: (1) a bucket became publicly readable last week, (2) a VM is running a process that behaves like a cryptominer, (3) a user granted a sensitive role yesterday to a Google group that has external members. Which pairing of the observation with the Security Command Center capability that most directly detects it is correct?

choices.text: Observation 1 by Security Health Analytics, observation 2 by Virtual Machine Threat Detection, observation 3 by Event Threat Detection
Observation 1 by Event Threat Detection, observation 2 by Security Health Analytics, observation 3 by Virtual Machine Threat Detection
Observation 1 by Virtual Machine Threat Detection, observation 2 by Event Threat Detection, observation 3 by Security Health Analytics
All three by Security Health Analytics, because it is the only service that writes findings about resources

stem: A regulated company wants its audit logs protected from workload administrators, because project owners could delete logs of their own actions. Which TWO controls form the best logging architecture? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Route logs to a Pub/Sub topic in each workload project so teams can subscribe to their own events
Give each project owner the Logging Admin role on their own project so they can manage retention to meet their needs
Keep logs in each project's `_Default` bucket and rely on a long retention period to protect them
Restrict that project's IAM so only the security team can administer sinks, buckets and retention, and lock the destination bucket
Create organization-level aggregated sinks that route audit logs to a dedicated logging project in the security folder

stem: Compliance requires audit logs to be kept seven years at the lowest storage cost. Logs are read rarely, during audits, and auditors can wait hours for results. Tampering must be prevented. Which destination fits best?

choices.text: A Cloud Storage bucket with a locked retention policy, with the sink's writer identity allowed to create objects
A BigQuery dataset in the workload project with default settings, so analysts can query at any time with SQL and the data never needs to be restored
The `_Default` log bucket with its default retention, since it keeps logs long enough for audits
A Pub/Sub topic with long message retention, since subscribers can replay messages for seven years

stem: A sink to a Pub/Sub topic in a restricted environment stops delivering entries. The sink shows `topic_region_not_allowed` configuration errors and log entries are dropped. The topic has message storage and in-transit restrictions applied. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Grant the writer identity the Owner role on the topic, because the error means that its permissions are too low
Switch the sink to a regional service endpoint for Pub/Sub, so the restriction is evaluated in the topic's region
Route to a Pub/Sub topic that has no in-transit restrictions, since sinks to topics with in-transit restrictions are not supported
Increase the topic's message retention so dropped entries are kept until the restriction is lifted

stem: A project sink routes Admin Activity logs to a central security project (the sink destination type is a project). The security team searches the central project's Logs Explorer and finds none of these entries stored, although routing works. What explains this and how is it fixed?

choices.text: The central project's built-in sinks exclude those routed entries; update its `_Default` sink or add a custom sink
Routed entries are held until the source project's Owner approves a replication request in the destination project
Projects accept routed entries as aggregated copies, so the sink has to be recreated at folder level before storage
The destination project's buckets keep routed entries for 24 hours, so a longer retention must be set on its buckets

stem: A company runs analytics in BigQuery. A security architect lists responsibilities under the shared responsibility model. Which TWO remain with the customer? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Maintaining the hypervisor layer under the managed service
Securing the physical data centers that store BigQuery data
Patching the operating systems of the hosts that run BigQuery query processing
Deciding which columns hold personal data and protecting them with appropriate controls
Granting dataset and table access to the right principals through IAM

stem: A function deployed to Cloud Run functions bundles an open-source library in which a critical vulnerability is announced. The business unit assumes that Google patches it because the platform is fully managed. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Google patches every library that runs on its managed serverless platforms, including dependencies the customer packaged into the function
The customer owns the function's code and dependencies, so it must update the library and redeploy; Google patches the platform
Google owns the vulnerability, but the customer must open a support case so that the fix is applied to its function
The vulnerability is the responsibility of the library's maintainers, so neither Google nor the customer must act

stem: A payment processor must determine which of its Google Cloud environments are in scope for a card-data security standard. It has 80 projects. Cardholder data is stored in one database project, processed by two application projects and reached by administrators through a Shared VPC host project. Marketing projects in a separate folder have no network or IAM path to these systems. What is the best way to scope the environment?

choices.text: Put only the database project in scope, since the other projects hold no stored cardholder data and cannot be assessed
Define scope by project name prefix, which auditors accept as sufficient evidence because projects are tagged by naming convention
Map data flows and connectivity from the cardholder data store, include what stores, processes or reaches it, and isolate it in a folder
Treat all 80 projects as in scope, because every project belongs to one organization and an organization administrator can reach it

stem: An auditor asks for evidence that the physical security of the data centers hosting the customer's Compute Engine VMs meets a regulation. How should the security engineer respond?

choices.text: Provide Google Cloud's compliance reports as evidence of inherited controls, plus the customer's own evidence for its configured controls
State that physical security is outside the audit, because the customer has no responsibility for infrastructure
Provide the project's IAM policy, which proves physical access is limited to authorised people
Request an on-site datacenter inspection from Google for the customer's own auditors, since only a physical audit can prove the controls

stem: A service account key for a production project is found in a public code repository and used to read customer data. Management asks, "Isn't this Google's incident, since the cloud was breached?" How should the security engineer classify and handle it?

choices.text: It is a customer-side credential failure: the customer revokes the key, reviews audit logs and runs its plan, asking Google about platform questions
It is Google's incident, because stolen credentials mean the platform failed to protect its identities
It is outside any responsibility model, so nobody is accountable until the cause has been formally classified by an external regulator
It is a shared incident, so the customer must wait for Google's investigation before it disables the key

stem: A CIO says: "We have shared responsibility documents, but we still make misconfigurations because there are too many services and settings." Which Google Cloud approach addresses this beyond the shared responsibility model?

choices.text: Transferring all responsibility to Google by moving every workload to SaaS offerings
Shared responsibility with a longer document that lists every setting the customer must decide in every service it uses
Shared fate: Google provides secured landing zones, opinionated guidance, attested infrastructure code and risk-sharing options
Disabling configuration options so that customers cannot change settings in any service

stem: A healthcare company runs a legacy app on-premises, new services on Compute Engine and GKE, and analytics in BigQuery, with data moving between them. Its security lead wants to document responsibilities for compliance. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Document responsibilities once per vendor, applying Google's general shared responsibility statement to each service
Build a responsibility matrix per service and per interaction between services, on-premises systems included
Document the BigQuery and GKE parts in detail, since managed services carry the largest and least clear customer share
Rely on Google's compliance reports, since workloads in its data centers inherit Google's certifications for their controls

stem: A payment processor is preparing for an annual card-industry assessment of a new workload on Google Cloud. The assessor asks who is accountable for the physical security of the data centers and for the firewall rules protecting the workload's VMs. Which approach to the evidence request is correct?

choices.text: Provide your own firewall configuration for both items, because only the customer's own environment can be audited under the assessed standard
Ask Google to provide the firewall rule evidence for the VMs, since network controls inside a project are operated by the provider
Provide Google's independent audit reports for both items, because the cloud provider's certifications cover every control that sits on its infrastructure
Provide Google's independent audit reports from the compliance resource center for the physical controls, and your own firewall configuration evidence for the VMs

stem: A security engineer is about to create an Assured Workloads folder in an organization where Access Transparency has never been turned on. Which TWO statements about creating the folder are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Creation fails until an administrator has manually enabled Access Transparency for the organization
Choosing a Free tier control package adds the personnel support restrictions that Premium packages provide
The folder can be created only as a direct child of the organization node, never beneath another folder
The organization chosen for the folder cannot be changed later, so the choice must be correct at creation
Access Transparency is enabled automatically for the organization, and projects created or moved into the folder use it

stem: A Swiss bank wants a local, trusted partner to manage its encryption keys, access justifications and audits, in addition to having data residency enforced. Which kind of Assured Workloads control package family fits this requirement?

choices.text: Sovereign Controls by Partners, which are operated and managed by a partner and include enhanced sovereignty controls
Regulatory data boundaries, which each address one named statute and are managed by Google only
Free-tier data boundaries, which add partner-operated key management whenever the Cloud KMS key location is set to the bank's country
Regional data boundaries, which restrict resource locations and optionally personnel support access

stem: A Canadian provider has chosen the Canada Data Boundary control package for a folder, but its contract also requires that first-level and second-level support staff be physically in Canada and legally eligible to work there. Cost review is strict. What should the security engineer recommend?

choices.text: Create the folder with the Canada Data Boundary package and enforce support staff location through a resource locations organization policy on the folder
Keep the Canada Data Boundary package, because every regional boundary already restricts which staff handle support cases in the country
Use the Canada Data Boundary and Support package, which adds support personnel controls, and plan for the premium tier and Assured Support
Use the Canada Data Boundary package and enable Access Transparency, because the logs make non-Canadian support access technically impossible to occur

stem: A team already runs a patient-records project in the shared development folder. Compliance wants it brought under the Data Boundary for Criminal Justice Information Systems (CJIS) control package. A junior engineer proposes simply creating an Assured Workloads folder and moving the project in. What should the security engineer do first?

choices.text: Delete the project and rebuild it in the new folder, because projects cannot be moved into Assured Workloads folders
Analyze the project against the package, fix any resources that do not meet its requirements, and then move it into the new folder
Move the project immediately, because the folder's controls retroactively relocate and re-encrypt every existing resource
Create the folder under a different organization that is dedicated to regulated workloads, then link the project to it by changing billing

stem: A defense contractor creates an Assured Workloads folder with the Data Boundary for ITAR package. Developers ask why they cannot find any encryption keys after setup completes. Which statement describes how Assured Workloads handles keys for this package?

choices.text: It generates one customer-managed key per supported service automatically and hands the key IDs to the developers working in the folder
It stores customer-managed keys in the same project as the workload resources so that developers can rotate them without raising requests
It leaves key management out entirely, because the platform's default encryption alone satisfies the package without customer-managed keys at all
It mandates customer-managed keys and provisions a separate key project and key ring, but administrators create or import the keys themselves

stem: A platform administrator widened the resource locations constraint on an Assured Workloads folder to include a non-compliant region so a pilot could start. The next morning the compliance team sees an alert from Assured Workloads monitoring. After the pilot is moved back to a compliant region, what is the correct way to close out the finding?

choices.text: Restore the package's compliant policy value and remediate resources so the violation is resolved; use an exception only for an accepted deviation
Disable monitoring on the folder, because the monitoring that raised the violation is also what keeps the violation open until someone turns it off
Remove the Assured Workloads folder and recreate it, because a violation can only ever clear when the workload is rebuilt on a new folder
Set the violation status to exception with a short note, which is treated by auditors as the same as restoring the compliant policy value

stem: Who is emailed by default when an Assured Workloads folder raises an organization policy violation, and what should the cloud security team do so its analysts are notified at the same time?

choices.text: Nobody is emailed unless a Pub/Sub topic is created, so the team should subscribe to a topic
Members of the Legal category in Essential Contacts receive it, so the team should also be added to that category
Members of the Technical category in Essential Contacts receive it, so the team should use the technical contact
The folder's creator receives the email, so the security team should be added as folder owners

stem: A bank's security operations team needs to view Assured Workloads violations across the organization, while a compliance lead must be able to record exceptions for accepted deviations. Following least privilege, which TWO role grants on the organization meet these needs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Organization Policy Administrator to the compliance lead, because policy administrators own the exception workflow
Logs Viewer to the compliance lead alone, because exceptions are recorded in audit logs
Assured Workloads Editor to the compliance lead, which carries the permission to update violations with an exception
Assured Workloads Administrator to the security operations team, so analysts can both read violations and change workloads
Assured Workloads Reader to the security operations team, which allows listing and reading violations

stem: A regulated customer enrolled BigQuery in Access Approval. A Customer Care engineer viewed a table name and a dataset's access control list during a case, and the approvers received no approval request. The auditor calls this a control failure. How should the security engineer respond?

choices.text: Explain that viewing BigQuery table names, dataset names and ACLs might not generate requests, while viewing data still produces Access Transparency logs
Re-enroll BigQuery with the GA-only option, because only that option generates requests for read-only access paths
Explain that BigQuery is a Preview service for Access Approval, so no requests are generated for any access to it
Agree, because Access Approval blocks every kind of Google access to BigQuery, so a missing request proves a defect that must be reported to Google

stem: A federal agency contractor creates an Assured Workloads folder with the Data Boundary for Impact Level 4 (IL4) package. The architect asks whether customer-managed keys are mandatory, as they are for the ITAR package. Which statement is accurate?

choices.text: Yes, IL4 mandates CMEK exactly as ITAR does, and a separate key management project is always created for the folder
No, CMEK is optional for IL4, so Google-managed encryption, Cloud KMS keys, Cloud EKM and key import remain available choices

stem: A deployment pipeline creates workloads through the Assured Workloads API using hard-coded compliance regime values written before mid-2025. A reviewer notes that several control package names, such as Australia Regions, have since been renamed. How should the security engineer treat this?

choices.text: Ignore it, since a renamed package no longer matters to the API
Pause all use of Assured Workloads until Google republishes the package under its original name again
Update the API values and documents to the new names; only names changed, not functionality
Treat it as a new control package with different guarantees and redesign every existing folder from scratch

stem: A hospital group chooses the US Data Boundary for Healthcare and Life Sciences package and wants to understand why some Google Cloud services are not in its supported products list. Which TWO requirements must each in-scope service meet under this package? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A dedicated physical host so no other customer shares the hardware
Automatic deletion of all patient data after thirty days
Availability in at least one region on every continent
Support for customer-managed encryption keys in Cloud KMS
Support for VPC Service Controls

stem: A policy review finds that the resource locations organization policy on the EU folder is enforced, yet an auditor spots a Compute Engine global address and several buckets created before the policy was set. The auditor calls this a residency failure. How should the security engineer respond?

choices.text: Disable the constraint, since it is known to be incompatible with resources that have a location
Explain the scope: it governs new resources that support location choice, not pre-existing or global ones, and is not a storage commitment
Replace the constraint with an organization policy that allows only global resources, which then covers every existing resource retroactively as well
Agree, because the constraint is a data storage commitment and any resource outside the allowed list proves a breach

stem: A legal team states that residency obligations cover the customer's content and also billing records, resource names and labels. The engineer must explain what Assured Workloads data residency covers. Which is the most accurate statement?

choices.text: Residency applies to all services in a project regardless of whether any given service can be configured for a data location at all
Residency covers every byte generated about the account, including billing records, resource identifiers and labels, in the selected region only
Commitments cover Customer Data at rest in location-configurable services, while billing data, identifiers and labels follow the geography documentation
Residency covers only the data in use in memory during processing and gives no assurance at all for data at rest in storage

stem: A company in a regulated sector wants to restrict every project in a folder to an approved list of Google Cloud services. A change here will take effect on all access to in-scope resources immediately, and some teams are unready. Which approach reduces the chance of an outage during rollout?

choices.text: Mix an allowlist and a denylist in the same policy so that unknown services are caught in both ways at once
Include IAM, Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring in the allowlist first, because the constraint blocks them unless they are named
Enforce the Restrict Resource Service Usage allowlist at the organization in one step, because the constraint only ever affects newly created resources
Use tags to conditionally enforce it on selected projects first, then widen, treating allowlist and denylist as exclusive modes

stem: Which TWO items does an Access Transparency log entry record about an action taken by Google personnel on a customer's data? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The physical location, employing entity and job category of the accessor
A copy of the customer content that was viewed, for later audit
The encryption algorithm that protected the customer content
The customer's own administrators who approved the action beforehand in every case
The reason for the action, expressed as a justification

stem: A security engineer tries to configure Access Approval on a new organization and is unable to continue. The organization has not enabled the log-based visibility product that Access Approval builds on. Which sequence satisfies the documented requirements?

choices.text: Enable Access Transparency for the organization, then enable Access Approval and grant the approver role to named administrators
Enable Access Approval first, then enable Access Transparency afterward so that earlier approvals can be logged retroactively
Create an Assured Workloads folder first, because Access Approval can only be enabled inside one
Grant the approver role only; Access Approval needs no enablement and applies to all services by default

stem: A Google support engineer requested access to a customer's BigQuery data for a case. The customer's approvers were on leave and no one responded. A manager worries that the lack of an answer might let access through. What actually happens?

choices.text: Access proceeds after an hour, because silence is treated as consent for support cases
Access proceeds once the support case is escalated, because case priority overrides the approval step
Access is denied only if an administrator dismisses the request, so someone has to act in order to deny it and record the refusal
Access stays denied, and the request is dismissed automatically if not approved within 14 days or before it expires

stem: An organization enrolls in Access Approval with the default option and later learns its regulator expects only generally available services to be in scope for approval requests. Which enrollment choice meets this?

choices.text: Disable Access Transparency, which narrows Access Approval to GA services
Enroll all services manually one at a time, because GA-only enrollment does not exist
Select the option that enables Access Approval only for services in the GA launch stage, which also covers future GA services
Keep the default option, which covers only GA services unless Preview services are separately enabled in another setting of the organization

stem: A customer uses an Assured Workloads folder whose package restricts Google personnel to a specific country. A support engineer from outside that country sends an Access Approval request whose location parameter is global. How is the request evaluated?

choices.text: The Access Approval request conditions override the package, so the global location is accepted if the customer approves it, whoever the engineer is
The package's personnel assurances apply first and the request's parameter is secondary, so personnel outside the boundary are not enabled
The request is converted into an exception on the Assured Workloads folder
Both rules are merged and the broader location is used, because the less restrictive control wins

stem: A European bank requires that no Google administrator access to its data can ever be approved automatically, even during an outage. Which statement about Access Approval auto-approval is correct?

choices.text: Outage requests may be auto-approved and logged as auto approved, except under EU Data Boundary with Access Justifications or Sovereign Controls by Partners
Auto-approval does not exist at all, so every Google request always waits for a named approver before access
Auto-approval can be disabled on any folder by clearing the Access Transparency setting for that folder
Auto-approval applies only to Preview services and is disabled whenever enrollment is limited to GA services in the organization or in any single folder

stem: An EU insurer wants evidence for each use of its customer-managed keys by Google systems or personnel, with a reason, and wants to approve or deny key use based on that reason. Which capability supports this, and what determines its availability?

choices.text: Access Transparency alone, because it provides a policy to deny key use by reason code
A resource locations policy on the key ring, which blocks key use when the reason is unknown
Cloud Audit Logs data access logs alone, because they supply and enforce a justification for each cryptographic operation on the keys
Key Access Justifications, with features and key types depending on the Assured Workloads control package chosen

stem: A regulated lender must scope its audit to as little of its environment as possible. It runs regulated loan processing and unrelated marketing analytics, and wants clear evidence of which resources are in scope. Which design best supports this?

choices.text: Keep all projects in one folder and label the regulated ones, relying on labels to define the audit scope
Define scope by billing account, since the billing account's projects always share the same compliance status
Place regulated workloads in dedicated projects under an Assured Workloads folder and keep unrelated workloads outside it
Create the regulated workload in the same projects as marketing analytics so that one set of controls covers both uses together

stem: A company federates 3,000 engineers into Google Cloud through a workforce identity pool backed by its SAML IdP; no user accounts exist in Cloud Identity. Access to the billing-analytics projects must follow two IdP facts automatically: membership in the IdP group finops-readers, and the HR attribute costcenter = 4711. A colleague proposes mapping google.display_name and google.email and writing IAM conditions on them. Which TWO configurations should the security engineer use instead? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Map google.profile_photo to a group marker URL and grant roles to principals whose profile photo attribute matches that marker value
Map google.display_name to the cost center value and write an attribute condition on the provider that admits only display names of 4711
Map google.email from the assertion and grant the role to that attribute in an IAM allow policy for each engineer who needs it
Map the IdP groups into google.groups and grant the role to the pool's principal set for the group finops-readers
Map the cost center into a custom attribute.costcenter and grant the role to the principal set for attribute.costcenter value 4711

stem: A helpdesk of eight people resets passwords and edits memberships of the groups used in IAM bindings. Today they share one super admin account, and an audit flags that this account could also change SSO settings and grant Organization Administrator. The CISO wants least privilege, individual accountability, and the super admin kept only for emergencies. What should the security engineer recommend?

choices.text: Grant each helpdesk member the Organization Administrator IAM role on the organization, which covers password resets and all group membership changes in the directory
Keep the shared super admin but enforce a security key on it and log every sign-in, so actions stay traceable to the helpdesk team as a group

Replace Token Creator with the Service Account User role on the project, which allows impersonation for testing but not access token creation
Remove the project-level grant and grant the group Service Account Token Creator on the etl-runner service account as a resource
Keep the project-level grant and require engineers to request deploy-admin through a Privileged Access Manager entitlement with approval

stem: A vendor's data-migration tool runs on Compute Engine, reads one OAuth access token from a file at startup, and cannot refresh it. Migrations run up to six hours. Service account keys are banned by policy, and the tool must use the attached service account mig-sa with no added standing privilege. The documented default maximum lifetime of a service account access token is one hour. What should the security engineer do?

Use Workload Identity Federation for the VM, because federated tokens exchanged through Security Token Service are valid for twelve hours by default
Create a key for mig-sa as a one-off exception and delete it after the run, because only key-based tokens can be issued with lifetimes beyond one hour
Set the token lifetime of mig-sa to six hours in the instance metadata, because the metadata server issues tokens with whatever lifetime the VM requests

stem: The organization enforces the managed constraint that blocks service account key creation. A quarterly scan still finds a new user-managed key on a production service account. Logs show an engineer generated a key pair on a laptop and attached only the public key to the account. The security team wants to close this path organization-wide without breaking workloads that use attached service accounts. What should it do?

Move every production service account into a single project protected by VPC Service Controls, which blocks external public keys from being attached
Shorten the key expiry constraint to one hour, so that uploaded public keys become invalid before they can be used to sign any request
Also enforce the managed constraint that disables service account key upload, since blocking creation does not stop attaching public keys

stem: Employees and contractors both sign in through workforce identity pools. Policy requires that contractor console (federated) and gcloud sessions expire after 30 minutes, while employees keep 8-hour sessions to avoid repeated sign-ins. Both groups use the same Okta tenant, and the security team wants the setting enforced by Google Cloud rather than by Okta, so that an Okta change cannot weaken it. Set the Google session length to 30 minutes in the Cloud Identity Admin console for a contractors organizational unit, and 8 hours for employees
Put contractors in their own workforce identity pool with a 30-minute session duration, and keep employees in a pool set to 8 hours
Keep one pool and add a second provider for contractors whose provider-level session duration is set to 30 minutes in the provider config

Grant Mina an unconditional custom role with project setIamPolicy, plus a deny policy that blocks setIamPolicy whenever the changed binding is not Compute Admin
Grant Mina Compute Admin on render-prod, because that role includes setting the project's allow policy for Compute Engine bindings and so lets her grant it onward

The organization has 900 projects and deep group nesting. The security engineer must produce an answer from current policies, not from past logs, and must cover every principal type. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Export Admin Activity audit logs to BigQuery and list everyone who has called SetIamPolicy on payments-prod during the last 400 days
Run a Policy Analyzer query for the permission on payments-prod with service account impersonation analysis enabled, through the API or gcloud
Use IAM recommender insights for payments-prod, because they list permissions each principal and service account used during the last 90 days
Run Policy Troubleshooter for each employee against payments-prod, because it reports both direct and impersonation-based access for every principal

stem: A shared project holds about 300 Secret Manager secrets for many teams, and new secrets appear daily. Team A must read only secrets whose names begin with team-a-, including secrets created later, without anyone editing IAM for each new secret. The security team prefers not to split the project or add tooling to maintain. Which configuration meets this with the LEAST ongoing administration?

choices.text: Grant Team A the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role on each matching secret, and run a scheduled job that adds the binding to every new team-a- secret

Grant Team A the Secret Manager Viewer role on the project, which allows reading secret payloads only for those secrets whose labels match the team's group name
Grant Team A the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role on the project with an IAM condition that matches only resource names with the team-a- prefix

stem: The tag key env, with values prod and dev, is defined at the organization and bound to the prod and dev folders, so projects inherit it. Organization-level IAM bindings give developers broad roles only where resource.matchTag on env is dev. A red team showed that a project owner in the prod folder attached env=dev directly to the project and gained those roles. An old rollout granted all engineers Tag User at the organization. Bind env=prod again at the organization as a default value, because a tag inherited from an ancestor cannot be overridden by a value attached to a project
Remove the tag binding permissions from the predefined Owner role at the organization, so that project owners can no longer attach any tag to their own projects

stem: Last month the security team enforced the managed constraint that restricts enabling serial port access on VMs at the organization. A scan today still finds 14 older VMs with serial port access enabled, and a network appliance vendor insists that its new VMs need the serial console for recovery. The team wants the appliance VMs as the only scoped exception. Which TWO actions should it take? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add the appliance vendor's support group to an IAM deny exception list, so the constraint no longer applies whenever those users change VM metadata

stem: A bank reaches Google APIs from its VPC networks only through restricted.googleapis.com, enforced with central DNS and routes. choices.text: The constraint that restricts allowed Private Service Connect producers, allowing only service attachments that live inside the bank's own organization

stem: A bank's internal-apps folder must never expose services to the internet, but its teams build internal Application Load Balancers and internal passthrough load balancers on GKE every week. The security team wants a preventive control that blocks any new external load balancer in the folder, needs no custom code, and must not disrupt existing load balancers during rollout. choices.text: A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the folder's projects with the Compute Engine API restricted, which prevents external forwarding rules

stem: A partner's service account must run a BigQuery job that creates a results table in a dataset inside an enforced perimeter. The security team built an ingress rule in the console with method selectors by permission, adding bigquery.jobs.create first and, in a second edit, bigquery.tables.create. The rule's identity, source and target project are correct, yet the partner's job is still blocked by VPC Service Controls. Add an egress rule that mirrors the ingress rule for the partner's project, because creating jobs inside a perimeter always needs rules in both directions
Replace the permission selectors with a method selector of "*" for BigQuery, because permission selectors are only evaluated for Cloud Storage

A pipeline in the private perimeter must copy files out of the DMZ buckets, but nothing in the DMZ may ever write to or read from the private perimeter, even if a DMZ identity is compromised. Both perimeters are in the same organization and access policy. Which design meets this?

Its source is the access level for the partner's office IP range, its identity type is ANY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, and it allows all BigQuery methods. The partner's job runs on a VM in the partner's VPC network. The security lead wants only that job's service account, from that network, reading data. What should change?

Name the partner job's service account instead of ANY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, use its VPC network as the source, and allow only BigQuery read methods

Change the identity type to ANY_USER_ACCOUNT, because service accounts from other organizations cannot be named in ingress rules of this perimeter

stem: Analytics VMs without external IP addresses run in a VPC network protected by VPC Service Controls, and DNS already maps googleapis.com to restricted.googleapis.com. The security team now wants the VMs unable to open any outbound connection except HTTPS to Google APIs through that restricted range, with the internet route kept for a Cloud NAT used by another subnet. Which TWO firewall changes achieve this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Deletion of the default internet route for the whole network, because egress firewall rules cannot block traffic toward a default route

stem: A bank's new policy says that every VLAN attachment created for Cloud Interconnect must carry traffic encrypted with IPsec, so that HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect is the only option. Network teams in several folders create attachments on their own. The security team wants this enforced preventively across the organization, with no change to the attachments that already exist. What should it configure?

stem: A SaaS provider must expose an internal API to 200 customer VPC networks. stem: A regulated folder must use only hardware-protected or external keys: software keys are forbidden for new keys and for new versions of imported keys. stem: A hospital deploys a custom model on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for online inference. Keep bq load --replace each night and recreate both row access policies in a pipeline step right after every load completes

stem: Under the regulated folder, constraints/gcp.restrictNonCmekServices denies storage.googleapis.com, and constraints/gcp.restrictCmekCryptoKeyProjects allows under:folders/kms-folder, which contains project kms-hub. stem: A bank's assistant on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform may ground answers only on the bank's own Agent Search data stores and its RAG corpus, and prompts must never be sent to public web search. choices.text: Add a VPC Service Controls perimeter around the AI folder, because grounding requests to Google Search leave the perimeter and are then blocked
Enforce the boolean constraint that disables Grounding with Google Search on the AI folder, since the sources list does not govern it
Add GoogleSearch to the denied values of the Control Grounding Sources constraint on the AI folder, because explicit denials override the gap

stem: After the monthly kernel patch window, Cloud Monitoring alerts fire on 280 production Shielded VMs: their lateBootReportEvent entries show policyEvaluationPassed false, and the changed PCR values match the new kernel recorded in the patch job report. Relearn the baseline on the 280 patched VMs through any project editor, and reboot the other VM to see whether its early-boot failure clears

stem: An Admin Activity audit entry from 03:12 shows principalEmail deploy-sa@prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com creating a firewall rule that opened SSH to the internet, and its serviceAccountDelegationInfo lists firstPartyPrincipal contractor-7@example.com. stem: A SIEM ingests audit logs through an organization-level sink, siem-feed, created by Terraform with the filter logName:"cloudaudit.googleapis.com" and a Pub/Sub topic in project sec-hub as destination. The sink's writer identity holds Pub/Sub Publisher on the topic, the sink shows no configuration errors, and sec-hub is not in a perimeter. The SOC wants every current and future project covered without per-project sinks, and the SIEM must keep reading the same topic. What is the cause and the fix?

The filter must list each project in a resource.labels.project_id clause; widen the filter so that project entries match the sink's conditions
The sink was created without including children; create an organization sink that includes children, same filter and topic, then remove the old one
Organization sinks route only organization-level entries by design; create a sink in each project and add one to the project factory for every new project

stem: To auto-remediate public buckets, a team created a Cloud Asset Inventory feed on the production folder with asset type storage.googleapis.com/Bucket, content type RESOURCE, and the condition temporal_asset.asset.iam_policy.bindings.exists(b, b.members.exists(m, m == "allUsers")), publishing to a topic that triggers a remediation function. The team must detect new public grants within minutes on every bucket in the folder, without polling and without granting the function broader permissions. What should change?

choices.text: Keep the feed as it is and recreate it on the organization, because folder-level feeds do not publish IAM changes on child resources
Keep the feed and add the asset type of projects, because IAM changes on buckets are reported as changes to the policy of the parent project
Keep content type RESOURCE and rewrite the condition on temporal_asset.asset.resource.data.iamConfiguration, which holds the bucket's IAM bindings

stem: A European retailer must permanently erase a customer's files from Cloud Storage within 72 hours of an approved erasure request. The bucket uses soft delete with the default 7-day retention (the documented range is 7 to 90 days, or 0 to disable soft delete), Object Versioning is on, and a lifecycle rule deletes noncurrent versions after 30 days. No retention policy or holds are set. Today the erasure job deletes only the live object. The security team wants soft delete to keep protecting all other data against accidental deletion. Which TWO changes let the retailer meet the 72-hour deadline? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Keep customer files in a separate bucket with soft delete disabled (0), and keep the default soft delete on other buckets
Set the bucket's soft delete retention to 3 days, so that deleted versions are purged in time to meet the 72-hour deadline
Add a lifecycle rule that deletes soft-deleted objects older than 3 days, so that the soft delete period no longer keeps them
Turn off Object Versioning on the bucket, which also purges the noncurrent and soft-deleted copies that already exist in the bucket
Have the erasure job delete every noncurrent version of the customer's objects too, not only the live version

stem: To meet a PCI DSS requirement that cardholder data never crosses networks unencrypted, the security team enforced the Cloud Storage constraint that restricts unencrypted HTTP access on the payments folder. That night a legacy uploader on an on-premises server fails: its logs show XML API requests to http://storage.googleapis.com signed with HMAC keys being refused, while a Python job using the JSON API client library and the Google Cloud console keep working. The vendor can change endpoint settings this week but cannot change the authentication method this quarter. Security will not relax the constraint or allow new key types. What is the correct remediation?

choices.text: Point the uploader at the JSON API over plain HTTP, because the constraint covers only the XML API and leaves JSON API requests untouched
Point the uploader at https://storage.googleapis.com with the same HMAC credentials, because the constraint refuses only unencrypted HTTP access
Exempt the uploader's bucket from the constraint with a tag-based conditional rule until the vendor can change the authentication method
Replace the HMAC keys with a downloaded service account key on the server, because the constraint refuses HMAC-signed requests from outside Google
